## Verdict: REJECT (a critical checklist FAIL on criterion 32 and two Important findings)

This PR is not ready to merge: `sqllens verify-memory` can exit with a message other than the rule-set one while a rule-set file is configured, a user ID ending in a newline is accepted, and some guard refusals write two WARNING log records instead of one.

Rule applied: rule 1 — a checklist FAIL at or above the threshold → REJECT

## Code Review Findings

### 🔴 Critical

- VC-111: FAIL (critical) — While a rule-set file is configured, `sqllens verify-memory` exits non-zero before running any case, with a message that it does not support rule sets yet. [src/sqllens/cli.py:581-596] — fix the code, or have the issue author amend this criterion

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  criteria.json read: valid list of {criterion,text}, criterion 32 is this item's; no sibling criterion mentions verify-memory ordering. Code: src/sqllens/cli.py verify_memory (head) checks, in order: (581-583) invalid --format -> exit 1 with a format message; (584-588) Config.load failure -> exit 2; (589-591) cfg.llm.api_key is None -> exit 2 with API_KEY_MISSING_MESSAGE; only then (592-596) cfg.rule_sets.loaded is not None -> prints VERIFY_MEMORY_UNSUPPORTED_MESSAGE ('sqllens verify-memory does not support rule sets yet; ...') and exits 1. run_verification (src/sqllens/eval/runner.py:131-134) also raises ValueError with the same message before any case runs. The main path conforms: non-zero exit, before any case, message says rule sets unsupported yet. Split of the guarding conditions: (a) bad --format: fires with a rule-set file configured, needs no fault, and the criterion's trigger does not exclude it; the exit is non-zero before any case but the message is not the rule-set one -> departure (no sibling names it). (b) llm.api_key None with rule set configured: same, exit 2 with the API-key message, not the rule-set message -> departure. (c) Config.load failure: arguably outside the trigger when the failure is the rule-set file itself being invalid (file not validly configured), but an unrelated config error with a rule-set file set also precedes. The departures only change which message is shown (still non-zero, no case run), so the impact is small, but under the grading rules an input inside the trigger yielding a different message is a FAIL.

  </details>

### 🟠 Important / Major

1. `src/sqllens/rule_sets.py` lines 394-402 (`_user_id`): the user-ID check accepts a value with a trailing newline. `_ASCII_DIGITS_RE = re.compile(r"^[0-9]+$")` is applied with `.match`, and in Python's `re` the `$` also matches just before a final `"\n"`, so `"7\n"` is served as user 7 instead of being refused as an invalid user ID (criterion 9). No test sends a newline-terminated value. The same pattern lets `permission_fingerprint` and `application_commit` (lines 53-54) accept a trailing newline, which only affects provenance fields. (raised by 1/6 agents)
2. `src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py` lines 440-454 (`RefusalRedactingRunner.run_sql`): some refusals write two WARNING log records instead of one. The redacting runner logs every `UnsafeSqlError` or `RlsError` that is not a `RuleSetRefusal` at WARNING, but the inner guards already log at WARNING before raising on their fail-closed paths: `safety/__init__.py:137`, `:215` and `:239`, `safety/relations.py:130` and `safety/whole_row.py:219`. Criterion 26 requires one WARNING record per refusal. (raised by 1/6 agents) [unmet-decided-criterion carve-out] <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=not-held limb-one=not-evaluated limb-two=not-evaluated; evidence: functional gap in the number of log records a refusal writes -->

### 🟡 Suggestion / Minor (9)

<details><summary>9 items</summary>

1. `src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py` lines 406-425 (`redacted_refusal_text`): a refusal message that matches no marker falls back to the read-only text ("only a single SELECT query is allowed") or the RLS text, so a reworded guard message or a new `UnsafeSqlError` (for example the read-only guard's "read-only guard errored") reaches the model with the wrong kind of refusal. Nothing leaks and the full reason is still logged. (raised by 2/6 agents)
2. `docs/internal/setup/config-loading.md` line 140: the sentence listing the sub-sections that set `extra = "forbid"` leaves out the new `RuleSetsConfig`. (raised by 1/6 agents)
3. `src/sqllens/rule_sets.py` lines 505-518 (`mysql_connect_kwargs` docstring): it does not say the function raises `ValueError` for a URL with no user or host, or a non-numeric port, which both callers depend on. (raised by 1/6 agents)
4. `src/sqllens/config.py` lines 762-774: `RuleSetsConfig` can hold `file` set while `loaded` is `None` (direct construction, `model_construct`, or assigning `file` after load), and every consumer reads `loaded is None` as "no rule sets", which fails open. No shipped path reaches this state. (raised by 1/6 agents)
5. `src/sqllens/rule_sets.py` lines 234-265: lists inside the frozen records can still be changed in place, `LoadedRuleSets` is a plain mutable dataclass, and `CatalogConfirmation.confirmed` is a public flag that can be set without its lock. (raised by 1/6 agents)
6. `src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py` lines 95-101: `RuleSetRefusal.kind` is a free `str` put straight into client text, so the promise that a refusal names no table or column depends on every caller passing a `KIND_*` constant; `TableRule.row_rule: Any` (`rule_sets.py:174`) likewise declares it accepts any value. (raised by 1/6 agents)
7. `src/sqllens/rule_sets.py` lines 287-288 (`_url_database`): it removes exactly one leading `/`, while `build_sql_runner` (`agent/factory.py:299`) uses `lstrip("/")`, so a URL path starting with `//` is compared against a different database name than the runner connects to. The load refuses; nothing is let through. (raised by 1/6 agents)
8. `src/sqllens/server.py` lines 371-393: no test drives a rule-set refusal through the MCP `query_database` tool; every test in `tests/unit/test_query_database_rule_sets.py` stops at `query_database_impl_with_widgets`. (raised by 1/6 agents)
9. `src/sqllens/preflight.py` lines 162-174 (`_check_rule_set_catalog`): the branch where the `information_schema` read raises something other than `RuleSetCatalogError` is untested. (raised by 1/6 agents)

</details>
